title: System Monitor
summary: A live look at the Raspberry Pi it runs on: CPU, temperature, memory, storage, network, processes and the power supply.
description: A full-screen monitor of the board it runs on, made for the deck's small screen and for touch. The overview shows the CPU load (and a bar per core), the temperature (amber from 70 °C, red from 80 °C, where the Pi starts to slow down), the CPU frequency, memory and swap, the load average, uptime, the space left on the system disk, the network and the power state: under-voltage now or since boot, frequency capping and throttling, decoded from the firmware's flags in plain words. Each line opens a page with a live chart of the last two minutes and the details: each core and the top processes by CPU, memory with the top processes by memory, temperature and power (the time since boot of the last under-voltage or throttling, the fan, the 5 V input on a Pi 5), every disk and its read/write rate, every network interface with its address, rates and Wi-Fi signal. A Processes page lists the top 15 by CPU or by memory; a System page names the model, kernel, OS and firmware. Values refresh every 1, 2 or 5 seconds (remembered). Read-only: it changes nothing on the system. Works on the Pi Zero 2 W, Pi 3A+, Pi 5 and CM5; the firmware flags need vcgencmd and the video group (without them the rest works). Needs a screen of at least 640x480 and a launcher with full-screen app support.
